h1: Class C Misdemeanor & City Ordinance Lawyer El Paso, TX
intro: A Class C citation for public intoxication, disorderly conduct, theft under $100 or a loose dog looks like a traffic ticket, but it is a criminal charge that follows you onto background checks. Attorney Robert Navar works to resolve it through deferred disposition or dismissal so it never becomes a conviction — and can later be expunged.
summaryHeading: A Class C citation is a criminal charge, not a parking ticket
summary: Class C misdemeanors are fine-only criminal offenses — no jail — but a conviction creates a criminal record that employers, landlords, licensing boards and the military can see.

Common El Paso Class C cases: public intoxication, disorderly conduct, theft under $100, possession of drug paraphernalia, minor in possession or consumption, open container, assault by contact, and city ordinance citations such as animal control violations.
Many Class C cases in El Paso Municipal Court can be resolved through deferred disposition: complete a short deferral period and the case is dismissed with no conviction.

A dismissed Class C case is generally eligible for expunction under the Code of Criminal Procedure (Chapter 55A, formerly Chapter 55), which orders the arrest and citation records destroyed. Flat fee from $59 in El Paso Municipal Court.

sections.heading: Why a Class C Misdemeanor Matters More Than a Traffic Ticket
paragraphs: Texas puts speeding tickets and public intoxication in the same legal category: Class C misdemeanors, punishable by a fine only. The officer hands you a citation, you get an appearance date, and El Paso Municipal Court handles it on the same dockets as traffic cases. That similarity fools people into paying the fine and moving on.

The difference is what the conviction says about you. A speeding conviction goes to DPS and your insurer. A conviction for theft, assault by contact, drug paraphernalia or minor in possession goes into the criminal history that background-check companies pull for jobs, apartments, professional licenses, security clearances and military enlistment. A theft conviction is a crime of dishonesty that can disqualify you from banking, healthcare and teaching positions.

Paying the citation is a guilty plea. Once it is a conviction, it is generally not eligible for expunction and can only sometimes be sealed. That is why the strategy on a Class C criminal citation is different from a traffic ticket: the goal is a disposition that leaves no conviction at all.

sections.heading: Animal Control and City Ordinance Citations
paragraphs: El Paso's city code violations are Class C offenses too, and the most common ones come from El Paso Animal Services: a dog running loose, no rabies vaccination on file, no leash in a park, a missing city license, or a bite or nuisance complaint from a neighbor. These citations are filed in El Paso Municipal Court like any other, carry fines, and create a municipal court record. Repeat animal citations can also lead to a dangerous-dog designation that is far harder to undo than the ticket.

Other ordinance cases we handle include noise and party complaints, junked vehicles and property maintenance, illegal dumping, vendor permits, and curfew violations for minors. Horizon City, Socorro and the smaller cities enforce their own codes through their own municipal courts, where the flat fee is $69.

Many ordinance cases resolve well because the underlying problem is fixable: show the court the vaccination record, the new fence, the repaired vehicle or the permit, and the prosecutor is often willing to dismiss. Where that is not enough, deferred disposition keeps the citation from becoming a conviction.

sections.heading: Deferred Disposition: How We Keep Class C Cases Off Your Record
paragraphs: When you hire us online or call 915-503-1600, we file an appearance and pull the citation and offense report. Many Class C criminal cases have weak evidence — no witness beyond the officer, no video, a store employee who will not come to court — and in those cases we ask for an outright dismissal first.

Where the prosecutor will not dismiss, Code of Criminal Procedure art. 45A.302 (formerly art. 45.051) lets the judge grant deferred disposition: you pay a court fee, meet any conditions such as an alcohol-awareness class or community service, stay out of trouble for the deferral period (commonly 90 to 180 days), and the case is dismissed with no conviction. Deferral is discretionary, but El Paso Municipal Court judges regularly grant it in first-offense Class C cases when an attorney asks properly, and you generally do not have to appear. Our goal is to pursue the best available outcome based on the citation, record, court and circumstances. Read more about how deferred disposition works in El Paso.

Our flat fee is $59 per citation in El Paso Municipal Court and $69 in the JP and area city courts, with additional citations from the same incident at a discounted add-on. If you missed your date and a warrant issued, our warrant recall fee of $35 applies and we ask the court to clear it before the case proceeds.

sections.heading: After Dismissal: Expunction Erases the Record
paragraphs: A dismissal does not automatically delete the citation. The arrest or citation record still exists at the court, at DPS and in the commercial databases that feed background checks. The Texas expunction statute — Code of Criminal Procedure Chapter 55, redesignated Chapter 55A — generally allows a person whose Class C case was dismissed after completing deferred disposition to petition for an expunction, which orders every agency to destroy its records of the charge. For most clients that is the real finish line.

Because we handled the citation, we already have the cause number, dismissal order and dates needed for the petition, which makes the record cleanup step straightforward. If a conviction already exists from an old case you paid years ago, expunction is generally not available, but an order of nondisclosure under Government Code Chapter 411 may seal it from most private employers.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes After a Class C Citation, and What to Send Us
paragraphs: Do not pay it, do not call the court to "explain", and do not sign anything beyond the citation itself. Keep the citation, note the appearance date, and contact us before that date. If your teenager was cited, the same advice applies — a juvenile Class C case follows the same path and the same deferred disposition and expunction tools apply.

When you hire us, send the citation (both sides), your driver's license or ID, any receipt, vaccination record, permit or repair invoice that fixes the underlying problem, the names of any witnesses, and any letter the court has mailed. Consultations are free, and we handle cases for clients across El Paso, Horizon City, Socorro, Canutillo, Vinton and Fort Bliss. Se habla español. faqs.q: Is a Class C misdemeanor a criminal record in Texas?
faqs.a: Yes. It is the lowest level of criminal offense and fine-only, but a conviction is a criminal conviction visible on background checks. Theft, assault, paraphernalia and alcohol convictions in particular are flagged by employers and licensing agencies.

faqs.q: Can I go to jail for a Class C misdemeanor?
faqs.a: Not as a sentence; the maximum punishment is a fine, generally up to $500 for Penal Code offenses. You can, however, be arrested on a warrant if you miss your court date, which is why we file an appearance right away.

faqs.q: What is deferred disposition for a Class C case?
faqs.a: Under Code of Criminal Procedure art. 45A.302 (formerly art. 45.051), the judge defers a finding of guilt for a period the court sets, commonly 90–180 days, while you complete conditions like a class or community service. If you finish without a new offense, the case is dismissed and there is no conviction.

faqs.q: Can a Class C misdemeanor be expunged?
faqs.a: Generally yes, once the case is dismissed after deferred disposition. The expunction chapter of the Code of Criminal Procedure lets you petition the district court to destroy the records. A conviction, on the other hand, generally cannot be expunged, which is why avoiding the conviction comes first.

faqs.q: Do I have to go to court for a Class C citation in El Paso?
faqs.a: Generally not. We appear on your behalf at the pretrial setting in El Paso Municipal Court or the JP and city courts. You would only need to appear if the case went to trial or the judge required it, and we would tell you in advance.

faqs.q: What does it cost to hire a lawyer for a Class C misdemeanor?
faqs.a: Our flat fee is $59 per citation in El Paso Municipal Court and $69 in JP and area city courts, plus $35 if a warrant has issued. Court fees for deferred disposition are paid to the court and vary by case. You can hire us online in a few minutes.
